title: The inference economy: tokens are the new currency
oneliner: Every LLM call costs tokens, so route work by difficulty: small models for classification, large models for complex analysis.
says: Tokens are the new currency, and you need to know the inference economy - also called AI FinOps. The money you spend on tokens to call LLMs or SLMs matters. His rule: use small language models strategically for classification-type work, and reserve large language models for complex analysis. That is how you save money on token spend.
explained: This is the cost architecture of AI in one reel. Training a model is a one-time capital expense; inference is the meter that runs forever. Every prompt and every response is billed in tokens, so an architecture that sends trivial tasks to a frontier model is a standing leak of money.

The routing rule is the practical core. Classification - is this email spam, which team owns this ticket - is easy, and small language models do it at a fraction of the price and latency. Complex multi-step analysis is where large models earn their cost. In mature platforms this routing lives in the inference gateway he details in Season 1, and the savings compound across every application on the platform. This is also why his Season 2 platform treats model selection as a governed, centralized decision instead of every team improvising.
takeaway: Design a model-routing rule into every AI feature: easy tasks to small models, hard tasks to large ones. Token spend is an architecture decision.
